key_insight: A transverse liquid n-heptane jet can initiate and stabilize an oblique detonation wave only within a narrow momentum window, with too little jet momentum failing to ignite and too much momentum destabilizing the detonation.
engineering_relevance: The results define a practical control map for scramjet-like combustors, showing how jet momentum and inlet-pressure fluctuations can be tuned to maintain stable detonation-based combustion.
method: Computational study of a confined model combustor with liquid n-heptane inflow and a transverse liquid n-heptane jet
Systematic variation of the jet-to-inflow momentum ratio, J, under steady and oscillatory inlet-pressure conditions
Identification of combustion regimes from the resulting shock/detonation structures
evidence_signal: The abstract reports regime transitions across multiple jet strengths, from no ODW to local near-normal detonation, standing ODW systems, wall-coupled ODW-Mach-stem configurations, and eventual detonation expulsion under excessive jet momentum.
watch_item: The stabilization mechanism appears to have a finite operating window, so the jet can lose effectiveness when momentum is too high or pressure fluctuations push the system outside the admissible regime.
paper_title: Liquid-fueled Oblique Detonation Stabilized by a Transverse Jet
